alternatives_considered: equivalence - This could capture the structural correspondence between local and global data, but was rejected because the convergence emphasizes computational procedures and systematic determination, which are naturally expressed as functors between appropriate categories rather than just structural similarity.
decisions.reasoning: This convergence is fundamentally about how local data determines global invariants through systematic procedures, which is best captured by functorial relationships between categories of local singularities and global topological invariants. The supporting results (Atiyah-Singer, Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch, Morse theory) all involve functorial constructions that transform local geometric/algebraic data into global topological information.

Category theory provides the functorial framework to express how local data (singularities) systematically determines global invariants. Algebraic structures are needed to formalize local rings and their properties at singularities. Topology is required for both the global invariants and the notion of locality.

decisions.choice: We organize local singularities into a category and construct a functor to the derived category of coherent sheaves via local cohomology. The Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch theorem and Atiyah-Singer index theorem then relate local algebraic/analytical data to global topological invariants through characteristic classes.

decisions.reasoning: This formalization attempt highlights the significant gap between current Mathlib and advanced algebraic geometry. The proof requires complex algebraic geometry, derived categories, K-theory, and index theory - all largely missing from Mathlib. The three identified gaps in the original proof (functoriality, spectral sequence convergence, computational complexity) remain unaddressed.
